newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures settle flat to higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures settle flat to higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled flat to higher on Monday despite weaker prices in the western U.S. physical market tied to continued bearish demand/supply outlook, brokers and traders said.
"It was a technical move," said one West Coast trader. "There was support for COB at $15.30. There was good buying against it."

October California-Oregon Border (COB) futures finished unchanged at $15.42 a megawatt hour (MWh) after trading between $15.30 and $15.66. November and December COB ended up eight cents at $16.40 and $17.98, respectively.
October Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 25 cents at $16.10 after hitting a session low of $15.80.
November PV ended up 15 cents at $15.05. Active deferred PV contracts finished mixed, with May 1997 PV off $1.50 at $13.45.
The market sentiment remained bearish despite resilience showed by the front-month contracts today, brokers and traders said.
"I would expect it to test lower. There's no good fundamentals," said one New York-based futures broker.
NYMEX estimated 196 COB and 145 PV contracts were sold today.
